# Stitch visual system v2

**Status:** Frozen shared visual language — 2026-10-10  
**Source:** Whole-product placeholder baseline generated by Stitch.

This file freezes the **shared visual grammar**, not literal fixture content.

Product behavior and scope remain governed by:

`docs/project/product-definition.md`

## Character

Ara should feel:

- calm;
- feminine;
- modern;
- premium;
- approachable;
- editorial rather than generic SaaS;
- operationally clear in task-focused areas.

Public pages may be more expressive and image-led.

Booking, My Appointments, Manager and Staff pages should be more compact and task-focused without looking like a different product.

## Color direction

Canonical visual intent from the generated baseline:

- canvas: warm ivory / off-white;
- card surfaces: white / very light warm neutral;
- primary accent: muted terracotta / rose-brown;
- primary ink: warm espresso;
- secondary text: warm taupe/slate;
- borders: low-contrast warm neutral;
- success: muted herb green;
- attention: muted amber;
- destructive/cancelled: muted carmine.

Useful baseline tokens from the generated design snapshot:

- primary accent: approximately `#9E5642`
- deeper primary interaction: approximately `#7D3E2E`
- base canvas: approximately `#FAF8F5`
- card surface: `#FFFFFF`
- subtle inset surface: approximately `#F5F1EB`
- border/frame: approximately `#E6DFD5`
- primary ink: approximately `#2C2623`

Do not introduce a new palette during page refinement.

## Typography

Visual hierarchy:

- editorial display face for major public headings;
- clean highly-readable Persian UI face for body text and operational surfaces;
- restrained weight changes;
- clear Persian numeral treatment for price/time/duration.

The Stitch export uses Noto Serif / Noto Sans style fallbacks. Final production font selection is not frozen by this visual document.

Do not let generated pages introduce unrelated font families or oversized dashboard typography.

## Shape and surfaces

- subtle borders;
- restrained or near-flat shadows;
- medium radii;
- pill shapes only where semantically appropriate, such as chips/status;
- avoid giant rounded SaaS containers;
- avoid glassmorphism and glossy effects.

## Spacing

- generous editorial rhythm on public pages;
- denser but breathable rhythm on operational pages;
- consistent section spacing;
- consistent card internal padding;
- avoid both cramped operational grids and excessive dead whitespace.

## Public shell

Public/customer marketing pages should share:

- one consistent RTL header/navigation;
- recognizable brand mark;
- booking CTA;
- common content width/grid;
- common footer;
- editorial image treatment.

## Operational shell

Manager pages should share:

- one right-side RTL navigation shell;
- consistent page header;
- consistent search/filter controls;
- consistent list/table language;
- compact status chips;
- predictable primary/secondary/destructive actions.

Staff/Specialist pages should reuse the same operational grammar with reduced permissions/navigation.

## Components to preserve

During page refinement, prefer evolving rather than reinventing:

- primary terracotta CTA;
- secondary outlined/subtle action;
- destructive muted-red action;
- service cards;
- specialist/profile cards;
- image-led editorial sections;
- search field;
- filter controls;
- operational data rows/tables;
- status chips;
- price + duration metadata;
- summary/sidebar cards.

## Prohibited drift

Do not introduce:

- black/gold luxury styling;
- bright beauty pink;
- unrelated gradients;
- glassmorphism;
- dashboard KPI aesthetics;
- a second operational design system;
- excessive card nesting;
- new visual language for each state.

## Freeze boundary

This design-system freeze does **not** freeze:

- placeholder copy;
- placeholder images;
- fictional prices;
- fictional contact details;
- exact page composition;
- responsive layouts;
- edge states.

Those will be refined separately.

The purpose of this freeze is to ensure every next Stitch prompt improves one page/state while remaining recognizably part of the same product.
